draft.title: Half-life
card: Half-life is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay. The decayed nuclei become different nuclei, and the sample does not vanish.
Each isotope has its own half-life. It stays the same however large the sample is.
Decay is random. We cannot say when one nucleus will decay, but in a large sample the fraction decaying in a set time is predictable.
After one half-life, 1/2 of the original nuclei remain. After two, 1/4 remain. After three, 1/8 remain.
draft.remember: Every half-life, the number of undecayed nuclei is cut in half.

a.q: A sample has a half-life of 6 hours. What fraction of its original nuclei remains undecayed after 12 hours?
a.why: 12 hours is two half-lives. The amount is halved twice, so 1/4 remains. It is not 0, because each half-life removes only half of what is left, not half of the original each time.
a.clue: Count how many half-lives fit into 12 hours.

b.q: Lab A has 8 g of an isotope and Lab B has 2 g of the same isotope. Which statement about their half-lives is correct?
opts: They are the same, because half-life depends on the isotope
Lab A's is longer, because it has more nuclei to decay
Lab B's is longer, because it has fewer nuclei
Lab A's is four times longer, matching its mass
b.why: Half-life is constant for an isotope, whatever the size of the sample. Lab A has more nuclei, so more decay in each period, but the fraction that decays is still one half. Mixing up the number decaying with the time for half to decay is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Half-life is a property of the isotope, not of the sample.

b.best: They are the same, because half-life depends on the isotope

problems.detail: The clue 'Half-life is a property of the isotope, not of the sample' all but states the correct option, so students can answer without thinking about it.

check.summary: The card, answers and explanations are correct. The clue for question b practically gives the answer away and should be made less direct.

flags: Question b, other: The clue 'Half-life is a property of the isotope, not of the sample' all but states the correct option, so students can answer without thinking about it.
